title: The Note Under the Ice

plate.narration: A fold in the air shivers at the end of the passage. Salt wind slips through, though the glacier lies all around. A low note trembles under the rock. Something here is waiting for an answer.

goal.text: Find out what is ticking under the ice, before a goat does.

steps.label: Follow the herd's ears to the ridge
Find what is making the ticking

search.narration: You stay at the singing hall instead of taking the shelf path. The yeti herder waits at the door with the kid goat under one arm. The kid is eating her scarf. "My herd keeps stopping on the east ridge," she says. "Ears up, all pointing one way. Something under the ice is ticking. I want to know what, before a goat finds it first. Will you help me look?"

variants.text: The passage behind the singing hall is as you left it, and the fold is still awake. Out in the snow, the herder waves with the kid goat under one arm. Walk back to the fold, or search the glacier again with her?

back_at_fold.narration: You walk back down the passage. The herder's cairn still guards its mouth. The fold waits, wide and steady, with salt wind on your cheeks.

plan.narration: The herder points at the east ridge. "Soft snow up there. Haul the sled, or go light?" Her sled has a coil of rope and a lantern tied on. The kid is chewing the rope. "Strange melt this year," she says. "Strange melt, short hay."

plan_a.narration: You load the rope, the lantern and a bundle of hay. The kid climbs on the hay and will not get off. "Every hand on the rope," says the herder. "Hay is heavy when it has opinions."

plan_b.narration: You tie the lantern to your belt and loop the rope across your chest. The kid trots ahead. "Keep moving," says the herder. "The crust only holds you if you do not stop."

climb_a.prompt: Every hand on the rope! Haul the sled up the soft slope.
climb_a.narration: The sled sinks to its runners. The kid sits on top like a queen. "Pull," says the herder. "She will not."

climb_b.prompt: Scramble up the crust. Light feet, no stopping!
climb_b.narration: The crust creaks under your boots. The kid bounces ahead, light as a snowflake. "Show-off," says the herder.

climb_done.narration: At the top, the wind goes quiet. A line of goats stands on the ridge, ears pointed west, toward the hall. The kid joins them and points its ears too, very seriously. "See?" says the herder. "All day like this."

climb_slip.narration: The crust cracks, and you slide back. The kid bleats with laughter. The herder hauls you up by the rope. "Up you come, little snowball." On the ridge, a line of goats points their ears west, toward the hall.

ridge.narration: The ridge is bare ice and wind. A dark hole the size of a bucket breathes out a cold, hooting draft. "A goat once slept in there," says the herder. "He still brags." Tick. Tick. Tick. On your pack, the Listening Chime leans on its cord, not at the hole, but up the glacier toward the oldest ice. Is the hole the answer?

ridge_a.prompt: Lie flat, ear to the ice, and follow the ticking to its loudest spot.
ridge_a.narration: You lie flat with an ear on the ice. It is very cold. "Other ear next," says the herder. "Fair is fair."

ridge_b.prompt: Test every draft with a wet finger. Quick, the wind keeps changing!
ridge_b.narration: You lick a finger and hold it up. The wind changes its mind every few breaths. "Wind is like goats," says the herder. "Never listens."

ridge_chime.narration: You ring the chime over the hole. One clear note, not sour, no echo. "Just wind," says the herder. "I could have told you that. I didn't, but I could have." The hole is only wind in a tube of ice.

ridge_done.narration: The hole only hoots. The real ticking is west, toward the hall, and low, under the ice. You pack snow around the hole so no goat noses in. "One less worry," says the herder.

ridge_off.narration: The wind swings, and the hole hoots at you rudely. You lose the trail. Then the kid sits down right where the ticking is loudest: west, and low. "Good kid," says the herder. You pack snow around the hole so no goat noses in.

holes.narration: West of the hole, three snow mounds lie in a row, and the ticking jumps between them. The kid dives into one and pops out of another. "Watch the tail," says the herder. "Where does it end up?"

interaction.cue: Watch the kid dive between the mounds, then pick where it ends up.

onSuccess.narration: Right mound! The kid has its ear pressed to ticking ice, right beside your boots. It sneezes on them.

onFailure.narration: Empty! The kid pops out three mounds away, already sliding. "Wrong tail," sighs the herder.

onAssisted.narration: The herder points with her chin, and you all see it. Right mound! The kid is right beside you.

kid.narration: A gust shoves the kid sideways. It slides on its belly toward thin ice over a melt pool. The herder is too heavy to follow. "Kid!" she calls. The kid is having the best day of its life. How will you stop it?

variants.text: It is only an arm's length away. You found it first.

kid_a.prompt: Throw the rope loop over the kid's horns!
kid_a.narration: You swing the loop. The kid sees it and thinks it is a game. "It is not a game!" calls the herder. It is a game.

kid_b.prompt: Sing the low hall note so the kid turns toward you.
kid_b.narration: You take a breath for the low hall note. The kid's ears twitch. "Lower," says the herder. "Goats like it low."

kid_wing.narration: A winged friend leaps into the wind and glides over the thin ice. Everyone else keeps the rope ready for the catch.

kid_wing_check.prompt: Glide low and grab the kid, with the rope ready behind you.
kid_wing_check.narration: You glide low over the melt pool. The kid sees you and squeals. "Grab the scruff!" shouts the herder.

kid_done.narration: The kid pops into your arms and licks your chin with a very cold tongue. "Good kid," says the herder. "Terrible kid. Same kid." She tucks her lunch bundle into your pack. "For the climb. Do not tell the kid."

kid_off.narration: You miss. The kid slides into a soft drift and pops out with a snowy beard, very pleased. "No lunch for you," the herder tells it. She tucks it in her coat, where it chews her buttons, and keeps her lunch bundle there too.

crack.narration: West of the ridge, the glacier splits in a long crack. Steam curls out, smelling like warm wet wool. The ticking comes from below. A narrow snow bridge crosses it. "My herd goes the long way around," says the herder. "Safe, but slow."

crack_a.prompt: Rope up! Step across the snow bridge, light and quick.
crack_a.narration: The snow bridge is thinner than a pancake in the middle. "Light feet," says the herder. "Think of feathers. Think of lunch."

crack_b.prompt: Read the cracks and shadows. Find the safest curve around.
crack_b.narration: The long way curves around deep shadows and old cracks. "My herd's way," says the herder. "They grumble the whole time."

crack_wing.narration: A winged friend flies the rope over the steam and ties it to a rock. The others cross the snow bridge with a hand on the line.

crack_wing_check.prompt: Fly the rope across the steam and tie it fast.
crack_wing_check.narration: Steam fogs your eyes as you fly. "Left!" shouts the herder. "Your other left!"

crack_done.narration: On the far side, the herder counts heads. "All of you," she says. "My favorite number." Steam fogs everyone's eyebrows. The ticking is almost under your boots now.

crack_slip.narration: The snow gives way. You slide onto a warm, steamy ledge below. The herder hauls you up, grunting. "Heavier than a goat," she says. "Not by much." The ticking is almost under your boots now.

post.narration: Under a lip of ice stands an old yeti listening post: a pole topped with a carved ice cup, like a giant ear. "My grandmother's," says the herder. "She never found out what ticked. Put an ear in and tell me." Here the ticking is louder, and it has a beat.

post_a.narration: You hum the low hall note into the cup. The ice hums back, a little flat. The ticking answers a beat later. The herder's ears go up. "It is listening. Do not stop."

post_b.narration: You count against your heartbeat. Tick, tick, pause, tick. It repeats. The kid counts too, with its hoof, wrongly and very confidently. "Ignore her," says the herder.

post_a_check.narration: The herder joins your note, deep as a cellar. "Hold it," she rumbles. "Hold it until it answers."
post_a_check.prompt: Hold the low note into the cup until the ice answers.

post_b_check.narration: You draw the ticks in the snow. The herder sets a claw beside each mark. "My grandmother made marks like these," she says. "She never worked them out."
post_b_check.prompt: Find the pattern in the ticks before it changes.

post_done.narration: The pattern matches the song you learned in the hall: slow, slow, quick. The ticking is the hall note, answered from far below. "Under the hall," says the herder. "Of course. Grandmother always said the hall had a cellar nobody could find."

warm.narration: The herder sets out a little stove of warm stones. The kid falls asleep on someone's boots. "The tunnel below is too narrow for me," she says. "I'll go around by the hall's back door and meet you." She gives you a jar of glowing moss. "Mosslight. For dark places."

tunnel.narration: The tunnel mouth is a low arch of clear ice. Beyond it is dark. Your footsteps come back to you late, like a shy echo. "Don't get stuck!" the herder calls after you. The ticking goes on ahead. How will you find your way?

tunnel_a.narration: You run the lantern along the wall, a stretch at a time. Frost makes patterns, mostly feathers. One stretch looks like a row of little stitches.

tunnel_b.narration: Hand on the shoulder in front, eyes closed, you hum the hall note. It comes back from the left, then from lower down. The ice hums like a very large, very shy cat.

tunnel_star.narration: A starweaver breathes on the wall, and the frost sparkles. The ticking line shows up like a path of tiny stars. The others hold the lantern steady.

tunnel_moss.narration: You open the herder's jar. Soft light spills out, and the ticking line shines on the wall like tiny stitches. The moss fades as you go, and you tuck the empty jar away.

tunnel_moss_check.prompt: Follow the shining stitches along the wall.
tunnel_moss_check.narration: The moss glows brighter near the ticks, as if it likes them. "Follow the bright bits," someone whispers.

tunnel_a_check.prompt: Study the wall, stretch by stretch, and spot the line of ticks.
tunnel_a_check.narration: Feathers, feathers, stitches? "Is that a stitch or a feather?" somebody whispers. "Stitch," says somebody else. "Probably."

tunnel_b_check.prompt: Hum together and follow the loudest echo, hand on shoulder.
tunnel_b_check.narration: Hum, step, listen. The echo comes back from somewhere new each time. "Left," someone hums. "No, down."

tunnel_star_check.prompt: Read the starlit frost and lead the way.
tunnel_star_check.narration: The starlit frost glitters like a path of sugar. "Don't lick it," says somebody, just in case.

tunnel_done.narration: The ticks run along the wall like stitches, then turn down to a crack at the tunnel's end. "Found you," someone whispers to the ticking. There, the tunnel shrinks around you. You will have to squeeze.

tunnel_off.narration: The frost blurs into feathers and more feathers. You bump the same wall twice. "Hello again, wall," someone mutters. The third time, you feel ticks under your hand. They lead to a crack where the tunnel shrinks.

squeeze.narration: The crack fits one body at a time, and no packs. Through it, the ticking is louder. Cold air slides out, smelling faintly of salt. "Salt?" someone sniffs. "Up here?" Part of the roof looks loose. How will you get through?

squeeze_a.prompt: Chip the crack wider with the rope hooks.
squeeze_a.narration: You chip with the rope hooks. Tink, tink, crunch. "Gently," a muffled voice calls through the ice. It is the herder, somewhere above. "That's my hall!"

squeeze_b.prompt: Smallest first, packs on the rope, nobody stuck. Work out the order.
squeeze_b.narration: Smallest first, then the packs, then the biggest. "Who's biggest?" someone asks. Everyone points at someone else.

squeeze_brace.narration: A thornguard plants both feet and holds up the loose roof. The others edge past, one at a time, with the packs on the rope.

squeeze_slip.narration: A duskrunner slides through like a ribbon and ties the rope to a knob of ice. The packs go over the rope, and the others follow.

squeeze_brace_check.prompt: Hold the roof up while everyone edges through.
squeeze_brace_check.narration: The thornguard braces the roof like a table leg. "Quick," they grunt. "This roof is heavier than it looks."

squeeze_slip_check.prompt: Slip through and tie the rope on the far side.
squeeze_slip_check.narration: The duskrunner slides into the dark. "Rope coming!" they whisper. "Mind your noses."

squeeze_done.narration: The crack is wide enough now. As you edge in, ice chips pat down from the roof. It gives a long, low creak. "That's fine," someone says. "That's a normal roof noise."

squeeze_off.narration: The crack is only half as wide as you hoped. Ice chips rain on your heads, and the roof creaks. "Breathe in," someone says. Everyone gets frosty eyebrows.

squeeze_hold.narration: The loose roof creaks, rests, and creaks again. Crawl only while it rests. "Now," someone whispers. "No. Now."

interaction.cue: Wait for the creaking to stop, then crawl.

onSuccess.narration: One by one, you crawl through on the quiet, packs and all. The roof does not even sniff.

onFailure.narration: You crawl on a creak. The roof sheds a heavy shower of ice chips onto every head, and everyone comes through bruised and frosty.

onAssisted.narration: You count the creaks together out loud and crawl through on the quiet.

seam_back.narration: You come out in a small round chamber. One wall is smooth and warm: the back of the sealed seam, the crack in the singing hall's wall that hums when yetis sing. The ticking is loud as a heartbeat. The herder's voice comes faintly through the ice: "Don't break my hall!" Pry the seam open quickly? Or answer its ticking and see what it does?

seam_done.narration: You hum the hall note softly at the seam, and wait. The seam ticks back, quicker. Frost sparkles down the wall in a pattern, over and over. "It wants you to say it back," the herder calls through the ice. "Grandmother said the ice talks, if you're polite."

seam_echo.narration: The frost sparkles a pattern: tick, tock, tock, tick. The seam wants it said back. "Polite," the herder reminds you through the wall. Everyone sees the sparkles a little differently.

interaction.cue: Watch the frost sparkle, then tap the same pattern.

onSuccess.narration: The seam hums, pleased, but stays shut. A line of light runs to a crack in the corner, narrow as a cat door. It feels like being shown the way by a friend.

onFailure.narration: You get it wrong, and the seam sulks. It stays shut and cold. At last it slides a grudging line of frost to a crack in the corner, narrow as a cat door.

onAssisted.narration: You trace the pattern together. The seam hums, pleased, and a line of light runs to a narrow crack in the corner.

behind.narration: You slip through the corner crack into a narrow passage behind the singing hall. It smells of salt. Far off, the yetis in the hall hold their low note. "Smell that?" someone whispers. "That's the sea." Ahead, the ticking stops, and something shimmers.

variants.text: The ticking walks ahead of you now, like a guide.
Behind you, the pried seam creaks, sore.

passage.narration: The passage ends at a fold in the air. Beyond its shimmer, you smell salt wind and hear gulls. The light around the fold is called Riftlight. Then your pack starts to hum. The Listening Chime is ringing all by itself, a thin note, answering the fold's low one. Nobody touched it. "It's talking back," someone whispers. What will you try?

variants.text: When you step closer, the fold shrinks a little, the way the kid does when you grab too fast.

chime.narration: You strike the chime. It was already humming, and now its note goes sour, with no echo. "Not ready," someone says. "Orin said sour means not yet." In the quiet after, a lower note trembles under your feet.

variants.text: The chime answers with a clear note and an echo. The opening is still ready, and the way back is still there. Your first song was enough.

read.narration: Your starweaver studies the light. The others see only a shimmer. "What does it say?" someone asks. The opening hums back faintly. Nothing steps through, and nobody can name the place beyond.

listen.narration: You put an ear near the rock. Under the gull cries, a low note rises and falls. "That's our song," someone whispers. "The hall song. Down here."

look.narration: Frost lines run toward the fold like the spokes of a wheel, and every line ticks. Beside it, someone long ago scratched a tally into the stone, one mark for each visit. There are not many marks. "Somebody came here before us," someone whispers. "And never told."

beat.narration: The fold ticks, steady as a clock. The beat has an order, and everyone holds a clue. Which taps, in which order?

interaction.cue: Share your clues, then tap the beat in order.
clues: The beat starts with a slow tap.
Two slow taps come before anything else.
A quick tap ends the beat, with no rest.

beat_done.narration: Your taps and the ticking line up: slow, slow, quick. The fold brightens. A gull cries on the other side, very close. "It knows the hall song," someone breathes. "Who taught it?"

beat_off.narration: The taps tumble into a clatter, and the fold dims. A puff of cold air ruffles your hair. "Shh," says somebody. You stop and listen instead: slow, slow, quick. It is the hall note, answered. The fold brightens again.

cairn.narration: The herder squeezes in from the hall's wide back door, with hay in her fur and the kid under her arm. She sniffs the salt wind and steps back. "The sea. Under my glacier." She hugs the kid tighter. "My herd must never wander in there. Goats go through anything. How do we keep them out?"

cairn_a.narration: You and the herder stack blocks across the passage mouth, leaving a gap for people. She tests each block with her shoulder. "Solid," she says. "Like my grandmother's cooking."

cairn_b.narration: You tie the herder's spare goat bells across the passage mouth. A goat that pushes through will ring like a party. "Then I come running," says the herder. The kid tries to eat a bell.

cairn_smash.narration: A bigfoot lifts the biggest blocks. Smash, thump, thump! "Oh, I like you," says the herder. The others fit small stones into the gaps.

cairn_smash_check.narration: Your bigfoot sets the last broad block, and everyone marks a gap for travelers. "Not even the kid gets through that," says the herder. The kid looks offended.

cairn_done.narration: The passage mouth is marked. Goats will stay out, and travelers will look before they step in. The herder pats the cairn like a friend's head. "There. It can be as strange as it likes on the other side."

herder_say.narration: The herder finds a row of old tally marks scratched beside the fold. "Grandmother's," she says. "She found it, and never told." She looks at you. "Maybe your song wakes it. Maybe it wakes what waits beyond. Your road, not mine." She presses four coins from the hall's tin into your hand, and a small warm bead. "Keepers' fee. The bead was hers."

variants.text: "And you poked it," she adds. "Go gently now. It poked back."

herder_share.narration: She eats it in two bites and looks embarrassed. "The hay is not the only thing running low." The kid gets the crust, and then eats her glove.

footing.narration: The herder scuffs the floor and frowns. Meltwater has left a slick skin of ice sloping toward the shimmer. "One wobble, and somebody slides in feet first." By the back door lie old planks and a little grit. The kid stares at a drip, fascinated.

footing_a.prompt: Chip small steps into the slick floor, deep enough to grip.
footing_a.narration: You chip with your heels and the rope hooks. "Little steps," says the herder. "Goat steps."

footing_b.prompt: Lay the planks on the safest line, and grit the thinnest ice.
footing_b.narration: You lay the planks and sprinkle grit on the thinnest ice. "Not there," says the herder. "There. No, there."

footing_buy.narration: A young yeti trots up with a sack of grit and a sign that says GRIT. "Grit!" he says, in case you can't read. You spread it, and it bites into the ice. The kid eats a pinch and regrets it.

footing_done.narration: The floor grips your boots now. The herder stamps on it, then on the kid's tail by mistake, and everybody apologizes. "Sorry, sorry, sorry," says the herder. Nobody will slide anywhere by accident.

footing_off.narration: A boot skids, and someone sits down hard. The thump makes the fold shiver. "Bottoms are not hammers," the herder says, hauling them up, laughing. The floor is rough, but it holds.

decide.narration: The hall seam answered your song. Here the fold itself ticks to the beat of that song. The herder waits by the cairn, the kid asleep in her coat. "Sing to it, and see what it does," she says. "Or leave it sleeping, and come home. I won't think less of you."

variants.text: The fold already knows your voice. It answered you at the seam.
The fold flinched when you pried at the seam. It may not trust a loud note now.

hold.prompt: Everyone sings the low hall note and holds it to the end.
hold.narration: Everyone takes a breath. The fold leans toward you, the way the seam did. "Low and slow," says the herder. "Like the hall."

sing_wobble.narration: The note wobbles. Frost showers down every collar, sharp and cold. Then the herder hums the low part from the cairn, deep and slow. "Again," she says. "With me." You find your note. It is not tidy. It is enough.

sing.narration: You sing the low note. The ticking steadies. The fold widens, and salt wind brushes your cheeks. When you stop, it stays open. "You answered it," says the herder softly. "You didn't push it. You answered."

variants.text: You hum again. The opening stays just as wide. It does not need another note. It has stayed open since your first song.

test_open.narration: You strike the chime once more. A clear note, and then an echo, coming back through the fold. "A way there," says the herder, "and a way back." Beyond, shallow water ripples around mud. Cross together, or go back to camp first.

variants.text: The opening stays wide after your song. Salt wind and gull cries keep coming. You could fetch the Listening Chime from camp before you trust it.

ready.narration: You stand together by the fold. The herder's cairn guards the passage mouth. She sniffs the salt wind. "A coast, under my glacier," she says. "Things are moving that should stay put. What is moving them? Can anyone put them back?" Your chime hums. For a moment it leans past the fold, up the glacier, toward the oldest ice.

variants.text: Goat bells tinkle softly across the passage mouth.
The ice blocks stand guard across the passage mouth.

You stand together by the fold again. The herder's cairn still guards the passage mouth, and salt wind still blows through. Things are moving that should stay put. What is moving them? Can anyone put them back? Your chime hums, and for a moment it leans past the fold, up the glacier, toward the oldest ice.

leave.narration: The herder walks you back to the hall by the wide back door. Behind you the fold sleeps on, ticking. "Something down there answers our song," she says. "Who taught it? And why is the sea under my glacier?" The Cairnstep lead is still yours, and you can come back to sing the note later.

variants.text: Goat bells tinkle softly across the passage mouth.
The ice blocks stand guard across the passage mouth.

kid_scoop.narration: The kid is so close you can hear it chewing. "Now," breathes the herder. "Before it thinks."
kid_scoop.prompt: Grab the kid before it slides off.

post_off.narration: You lose the beat, and your ear freezes to the cup. Ow! The herder breathes on it until it comes unstuck. Then she reads her grandmother's old marks on the pole. "Slow, slow, quick," she says. "Like the hall song. Grandmother had it all along."

seam_pry.narration: You jam the rope hooks into the seam and lean. The ice groans. "Is it supposed to make that noise?" someone asks.
seam_pry.prompt: Lever the seam apart with the rope hooks.

onSuccess.narration: Crack! The seam splits a finger wide, and cold salt air rushes out. Somewhere beyond, something flinches, like a sleeper poked in the ribs.

onFailure.narration: The seam holds, then spits ice chips in your faces. A crack opens in the corner instead, and you squeeze through, stinging. Something beyond flinches.

hold_hard.narration: Everyone takes a breath. The fold shivers away from the first sound, like a goat that has been grabbed once too often. "Gentle," says the herder. "Gentler than that."
hold_hard.prompt: Everyone sings the low hall note softly and holds it to the end.

voiceGuide.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
voiceGuide.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.

npcVoices.Yeti herder: She/her, the glacier's goat herder. Slow, dry and fond; worries about hay and goats in that order. Quotes her grandmother, who kept the listening post. Short sentences.
